summary: Cypriot authorities closed the Ledra Street–Lokmaci pedestrian crossing in Nicosia on 29 February 2020 as a precaution against COVID-19. Ordinary pedestrian passage resumed on 4 June 2021, subject to health-document requirements. The closure concerned this crossing of the Green Line, which divides Cyprus, rather than every crossing or an internationally recognised border between states.

verification.notes: Checked actual barricades and pedestrian reopening; retained single-crossing and conditional-access scope.

summary: Switzerland extended its COVID-19 entry restrictions to its borders with Germany, Austria and France on 17 March 2020. Travellers needed qualifying nationality, residence or essential reasons to enter; goods and permitted transit remained allowed. Free movement for EU, EFTA and UK travellers was restored on 15 June, while restrictions on other foreign visitors continued. The separate restrictions at the Italian border had begun earlier.

verification.notes: Checked March 17 extension, excluded Italy onset, and limited June endpoint to eligible travellers.

summary: Denmark began refusing entry to foreign travellers without an accepted essential purpose on 14 March 2020 to limit COVID-19 transmission. At the German border, three road crossings remained available and ten others were sealed; citizens, residents, workers and freight retained exceptions. Access eased in stages during June, including limited reopening at Padborg and admission for eligible German visitors. The original 13 April end date was an announced deadline, not evidence of reopening.

verification.notes: Checked actual refusals, three versus ten crossings, freight exemption, and distinct June easing milestones.

summary: Poland restricted foreign passenger entry from 15 March 2020 to reduce the spread of COVID-19 and suspended international passenger rail services. Returning citizens and specified family, residence and work categories remained eligible, while freight continued. Ordinary movement across Poland’s internal EU borders was restored on 13 June. That change did not end restrictions at its external borders or establish when every international train service resumed.

verification.notes: Checked internal-EU endpoint; distinguished foreign admission and passenger rail from freight.

summary: Serbia tightened its COVID-19 border restrictions on 20 March 2020, closing passenger entry to citizens as well as foreigners while continuing to admit trucks and specially authorised travellers. Conditional admission was restored in May, using testing, isolation and permission requirements that differed between traveller groups. The remaining special admission and closure rules were removed on 22 May. These changes concerned entry into Serbia; departure remained possible.

verification.notes: Checked tightened onset, May 8 versus May 12 distinction, May 22 final rule change and inbound direction.

summary: Montenegro prohibited entry by most foreign passengers on 15 March 2020 to prevent COVID-19 transmission. Residents and freight drivers were exempt, and citizens could return under isolation requirements. On 1 June, the government reopened road posts closed for the pandemic and admitted visitors from countries meeting its health criteria. This was a selective reopening; the Vraćenovići–Deleuša crossing remained closed for separate construction work.

verification.notes: Checked foreigner-only ban, essential exceptions, June incidence list and distinct construction closure.

summary: Albania suspended ordinary passenger-vehicle travel across its land borders in March 2020 as part of its COVID-19 measures, while exempting goods transport. Official accounts place the restriction on 15 March but give conflicting starting times. Land borders reopened on 1 June, although public-transport restrictions remained. The reopening did not establish that every passenger service resumed or that neighbouring countries allowed reciprocal entry.

verification.notes: Retained onset clock conflict, formal land reopening and residual public-transport limits.

summary: Spanish authorities restricted nonessential movement at the La Línea–Gibraltar frontier during the March 2020 COVID-19 emergency. Travellers faced checks and refusals, while residence, work, essential travel and goods retained exceptions. Gibraltar residents were permitted to enter Spain by 10 June; an official statement confirmed unrestricted frontier flow in both directions by 10 November. The available reports do not establish exactly when each restriction ended.

verification.notes: Checked observed March restrictions and different later access observations without inferring continuous closure.

summary: The Czech government barred ordinary departures by citizens and residents from 16 March 2020 as part of its COVID-19 measures, alongside restrictions on foreign entry. Transport workers, some commuters and other authorised travellers retained exceptions. Permission for essential trips expanded in April, and ordinary departure became possible again on 24 April. Return requirements and neighbouring countries’ entry restrictions remained separate, so permission to leave did not guarantee a completed cross-border journey.

verification.notes: Preferred explicit domestic April 24 departure notices over embassy grouping with April 27 return rules.

summary: North Macedonia restricted entry by foreign passengers at its land crossings in mid-March 2020 to prevent COVID-19 transmission. Freight, diplomats and specially authorised travellers were exempt. Limited transit was permitted in June before ordinary land-entry restrictions were lifted on 26 June. The starting date remains between 16 and 17 March, and the earlier transit permission did not amount to a general reopening for visitors.

verification.notes: Checked March 16–17 bracket, exempt groups, transit milestones and June 26 admission endpoint.

summary: Norway restricted entry by foreign nationals from 16 March 2020 to limit COVID-19 transmission, while exempting citizens, qualifying residents and specified work, family and transport groups. A replacement legal framework took effect in July, with eligibility changing thereafter. The general restriction on foreigners’ admission ended on 26 November 2021; testing, registration and quarantine requirements continued until February 2022. The border was therefore never uniformly closed to every traveller throughout this period.

verification.notes: Checked initial and successor instruments; distinguished November admission change from February health-rule removal.

summary: Portugal and Spain restricted nonessential cross-border movement from the night of 16–17 March 2020 to contain COVID-19. Passage was channelled through nine authorised crossings, with exceptions for freight, workers, returning citizens and residents, family reunification, healthcare and emergencies. The bilateral restriction was formally lifted on 1 July. The two countries’ different local start dates refer to the same moment.

verification.notes: Checked reciprocal scope, authorised posts, exceptions and formal July endpoint; dates reflect time zones.

summary: Germany began rejecting travellers without an urgent reason at its Austrian, Swiss, French, Luxembourg and Danish borders on 16 March 2020 to curb COVID-19. Freight, commuters and other essential travellers retained exceptions. Crossing routes generally became available again in May, but tourist entry remained restricted. At the Austrian frontier, the COVID-related admission rule ended around 15–16 June; other frontiers eased separately, and migration checks continued.

verification.notes: Kept five-frontier onset separate from Austria-only duration and distinguished May route reopening from June eligibility.

summary: Hungary restricted entry by foreign passengers from 17 March 2020 as COVID-19 spread, while allowing Hungarian citizens to return and continuing goods and permitted transit. Exceptions expanded over time. Austrian, Czech and Slovak citizens gained unrestricted entry on 5 June; broader EU, EEA and Swiss access followed on 18 June, with separate arrangements for Serbian and Ukrainian travellers. These changes did not reopen Hungary equally to all foreign visitors.

verification.notes: Checked cohort-specific June easing and avoided treating original onset observation as entire continuous closure.

summary: Spain restricted nonessential entry across its French land frontier from 17 March 2020 to protect public health during the COVID-19 emergency. Spanish citizens, residents, cross-border workers and other necessary journeys were exempt, and goods transport continued. The restriction for ordinary foreign visitors ended on 21 June. Spain’s separate arrangements with Portugal lasted longer and are not covered by this endpoint.

verification.notes: Checked legal succession and France-only formal endpoint; retained inbound direction and exceptions.

summary: Belgium prohibited nonessential departures from 18 March 2020 during the COVID-19 emergency and explicitly extended the legal prohibition to arrivals on 3 April. Freight, cross-border employment and other essential journeys remained permitted. Family and shopping exceptions began to widen in late May, before nonessential travel with EU and Schengen neighbours resumed on 15 June. Border controls had begun before the later legal wording on arrivals.

verification.notes: Distinguished outbound and inbound legal starts from earlier controls; retained gradual exemptions and EU/Schengen endpoint.

summary: Russia restricted nonexempt passenger movement through land, rail and other surface border checkpoints from 30 March 2020, citing COVID-19 prevention. The national order included the Belarus boundary and restricted outward travel by Russian citizens as well as other passenger movement, while allowing transport crews and specified essential cases. It was repealed on 15 July 2022 after changing exemptions. That repeal did not remove separate wartime restrictions or neighbouring countries’ entry rules.

verification.notes: Checked national rather than Europe-only scope; treated repeal as end of legal regime, not universal crossing reopening.

summary: Hungary reintroduced restrictions on foreign passenger entry on 1 September 2020, citing imported COVID-19 infections. Citizens could return under quarantine rules, and justified travel and humanitarian transit retained exceptions. Land arrivals from six neighbouring territories were exempted in June 2021, with Ukraine added on 7 August. The remaining framework was repealed in March 2022, after these earlier land-entry changes; air-arrival rules had differed.

verification.notes: Checked territorial rather than nationality-based exemptions, August Ukraine addition and residual March repeal.

summary: France suspended arrivals from the United Kingdom through the Channel Tunnel on the night of 20–21 December 2020 following concern about a new coronavirus variant. The halt affected passengers and accompanied freight travelling to France; reverse travel and unaccompanied goods were outside it. Eligible passengers began crossing again on 23 December, followed by trucks and vans, under negative-test requirements. This was a conditional resumption, and queues did not immediately disappear.

verification.notes: Checked direction, operational onset range, actual December 23 resumption and tested eligible cohorts.

summary: Belarus restricted departure by its citizens and residents through western and southern land checkpoints from 21 December 2020, officially citing COVID-19. Work, study, medical, family and transport exceptions applied and changed over time. Air departures and the boundary with Russia were outside this measure. The government lifted the COVID-related crossing restrictions on 3 April 2022, although this does not identify the first outward journey through each post.

verification.notes: Checked outward citizen/resident scope, Russia and air exclusions and formal April endpoint; omitted unverified political motive.

summary: Sweden barred most foreign arrivals from Denmark from 22 December 2020 because of concern about a new coronavirus variant. The restriction included travel over the Öresund fixed link, but Swedish citizens, people living or working in Sweden and goods-transport personnel retained exceptions. The Denmark-specific entry prohibition ended on 31 March 2021. Negative-test requirements continued, so lifting the ban did not remove all health conditions on travel.

verification.notes: Checked inbound direction, exempt groups, special country-ban endpoint and separate testing requirements.

summary: Sweden restricted entry from Norway from 25 January 2021 following a coronavirus-variant outbreak around Oslo and concern about cross-border movement. Swedish citizens, residents, people working in Sweden, transport staff and urgent family cases retained exceptions. The Norway-specific prohibition was lifted on 31 March, while negative-test requirements continued. This restricted particular arrivals into Sweden rather than stopping all movement across the bilateral border.

verification.notes: Checked Oslo rationale, inbound scope, exemptions and March formal endpoint.

summary: Portugal and Spain again restricted nonessential land travel from 31 January 2021 to curb COVID-19, directing permitted journeys through designated posts. Freight, cross-border workers, emergencies and returning citizens or residents retained exceptions. General road-border travel resumed on 1 May. The Porto–Vigo Celta train also resumed a reduced service that day, but its full timetable returned later and river crossings followed separate arrangements.

verification.notes: Checked January application rather than publication date and kept road, partial rail and river endpoints separate.

summary: Poland closed the Kuźnica–Bruzgi road crossing with Belarus on 9 November 2021 amid the border migration crisis, citing the situation at the frontier. The closure stopped ordinary passenger and freight traffic at that post, with other crossings initially available. Passenger cars began crossing again on 17 November 2025. Freight and coaches remained excluded, and the later reopening of the approach road did not remove those border restrictions.

verification.notes: Checked actual car reopening, continuing freight/coach exclusions and distinct approach-road works.

summary: Ukraine suspended ordinary operations at listed crossings with Russia, Belarus and the Transnistrian segment of Moldova from 28 February 2022 following Russia’s invasion. The order covered passengers and freight while requiring provision for returning Ukrainian citizens. The Kuchurhan railway crossing was removed from the closure list in October 2023 and resumed work that autumn; this did not reopen the separate road crossing. Other listed restrictions continued, with humanitarian access varying over time.

verification.notes: Checked effective February 28 onset, returning-citizen exception and railway-only Kuchurhan change; avoided universal Transnistrian status claim.

summary: Latvia restricted nonessential entry by Russian short-stay visa holders at its external EU border from 19 September 2022, citing public-order and security risks linked to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Tourism and leisure visits were affected, while qualifying residents, family members, humanitarian cases and transport personnel retained exceptions. A replacement regulation in March 2025 continued the restriction. It limited eligibility to enter Latvia rather than closing the frontier to all Russian nationals.

verification.notes: Checked 2022 onset, 2025 legal succession, exceptions and inbound-only scope; no assumed reopening at scheduled expiry.

summary: Estonia restricted nonessential entry by Russian citizens using Estonian visas in August 2022 and broadened the restriction to short-stay visa holders on 19 September, in response to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The rules applied at Estonia’s external border, with exceptions for specified family, work, study, transport, residence transit and humanitarian purposes. The restriction continued under amended rules in January 2026, which also required prior permission for specified Russian diplomatic personnel and relatives.

verification.notes: Checked August and September stages plus January 2026 amendment; preserved short-stay and exempt-category limits.

summary: Poland restricted Russian nationals’ entry through its external road and rail border crossings from 19 September 2022, affecting ordinary tourism, business, sport and cultural visits. Specified residence, family and other authorised categories remained eligible, and the Border Guard could grant exceptional permission. Official guidance still described the restrictions in July 2024. This was an admission rule for particular travellers, rather than a closure of every crossing to all traffic.

verification.notes: Checked external surface-route onset and legal exceptions; retained dated confirmation without projecting current status or unsupported motive.

summary: Finland restricted entry by Russian tourists and tourism-related transit from 30 September 2022, citing security and international-relations concerns. Humanitarian travel and other permitted purposes retained exceptions. Replacement rules in July 2023 continued the restriction and tightened eligibility for business visitors, property owners and students; official guidance still described it in September 2025. These passenger-admission rules were separate from the later physical closure of Finland’s eastern road crossings.

verification.notes: Checked tourism and transit scope, 2023 replacement and 2025 confirmation separately from road-post closures.

summary: Poland closed the Bobrowniki–Bierestowica road crossing with Belarus on 10 February 2023, citing state security amid tensions over repression of Poles in Belarus. The closure affected passengers and road freight at this post, while other routes remained available. Traffic resumed on 17 November 2025 for cars, coaches and eligible freight vehicles registered in the EU, EFTA or Switzerland. The reopening therefore retained restrictions on other freight vehicles.

verification.notes: Checked attributed security/political context and actual selective reopening; not confused with narrower Kuźnica car-only opening.

summary: Lithuania closed the Šumskas and Tverečius road crossings with Belarus on 18 August 2023, citing security concerns including possible provocations involving Wagner personnel. Both posts handled light vehicles, and Tverečius also handled empty freight trucks; traffic was redirected to four other crossings. Later official listings continued to mark the two posts closed. The measure concerned these facilities, rather than the whole Lithuanian–Belarusian border.

verification.notes: Checked traffic types, named posts and official rationale attribution; retained later directory status without fabricated reopening.

summary: Latvia suspended the Silene–Urbani crossing with Belarus on 19 September 2023, stopping passenger passage and customs operations for imports, exports and transit goods. The Interior Ministry cited irregular-entry pressure and the need to redeploy officers, while Pāternieki remained available. An August 2026 ministry report still described Silene as closed. Plans to invest in equipment did not amount to reopening, and Pāternieki’s separate interruptions are not part of this closure.

verification.notes: Checked official stated reasons, passenger/goods scope and August 2026 persistence; distinguished investment and other-post interruption.

summary: Finland closed its road crossings with Russia in stages during November 2023, citing migration pressure and security concerns. Four posts closed on 18 November, three more on 24 November and the last on 30 November, while freight rail at Vainikkala continued. Vaalimaa and Niirala briefly reopened to actual traffic on 14 December; the other six posts stayed closed. The renewed closure the following day is a separate episode.

verification.notes: Checked staggered starts, actual December 14 passage and six-post continuation without bridging the reopening.

summary: Finland renewed the closure of all eight road crossings with Russia on 15 December 2023, after briefly reopening Vaalimaa and Niirala. The government attributed the decision to organised migration pressure and security risks. Passenger and road-freight passage stopped, while freight rail at Vainikkala remained outside the closure and asylum applications were directed to open air and sea entry points. Subsequent government statements continued to describe the road crossings as closed.

verification.notes: Checked renewed onset after brief opening, all-eight road scope, official attribution and distinct rail exception.

summary: Lithuania closed the Lavoriškės and Raigardas road crossings with Belarus on 1 March 2024, citing security, smuggling and sanctions-enforcement concerns. Vehicles could still use Medininkai and Šalčininkai, but pedestrian and cycle passage there was prohibited. Passenger boarding and alighting were also restricted at Kena and Kybartai railway posts, with exceptional permission possible; transit trains were not banned. Later reopening decisions for other posts did not reopen Lavoriškės or Raigardas.

verification.notes: Checked differentiated road and rail measures, Kybartai Russia route and later reopening scope.

summary: Norway began refusing nonessential entry by many Russian visitor-visa holders at its external Schengen border on 29 May 2024, aligning with partners’ response to Russia’s war against Ukraine. The rule affected tourism through Storskog, including travellers holding visas from other Schengen states. Specified family, work, study, residence and other authorised cases remained eligible. Storskog continued handling permitted traffic, so the measure did not close the crossing itself.

verification.notes: Checked external-border visitor categories, attributed rationale and continuing permitted Storskog traffic.

summary: Poland closed its remaining open road and freight-rail crossings with Belarus on 12 September 2025, citing security risks associated with the Zapad military exercises. The measure stopped ordinary passenger and commercial movement through routes including Terespol and Kukuryki. Road traffic resumed on 25 September, and the government restored the affected rail routes. Kuźnica and Bobrowniki, which had closed earlier for separate reasons, remained closed at that stage.

verification.notes: Checked additional remaining-route closure and actual road reopening; did not infer first-train passage or reopen earlier-closed posts.

summary: Estonia blocked the Värska–Ulitina road through Russia’s Saatse Boot on 10 October 2025 after reporting increased Russian personnel activity. The special transit route crossed Russian territory without ordinary border formalities and had carried vehicles and buses; pedestrians were already excluded. Travellers had to use alternative roads within Estonia. Later reporting still described the original road as closed while a bypass was being built, rather than recording its reopening.

verification.notes: Checked special vehicle-transit route, pre-existing pedestrian exclusion and original-road versus bypass distinction.

summary: Lithuania repeatedly restricted traffic at Medininkai and Šalčininkai in October 2025 after incidents involving smuggling balloons and aviation-safety concerns. Brief closures on 22 and 24–25 October were followed by a longer restriction from 26 October, with specified diplomatic, transit and return journeys permitted at Medininkai. Ordinary vehicle traffic resumed on 20 November, earlier than initially planned. Earlier pedestrian and cycle restrictions remained, and the brief reopened intervals are separate from the longer closure.

verification.notes: Checked separate short episodes, October 26 onset, October 30 policy transition and actual November 20 conditional restoration.

summary: Bulgarian nationalist activists blocked inbound passenger approaches at Kapitan Andreevo, Malko Tarnovo and Lesovo on 21 March 2017, opposing buses bringing Bulgarian citizens resident in Turkey to vote. The actions lasted hours or minutes and ended that day, with some other movement continuing. These were protest blockades rather than government border closures, and the activists’ allegations about voting did not establish that the journeys were unlawful.

verification.notes: Checked three distinct brief blockades, direction and attributed electoral claims; omitted poorly reverified freight exception.

summary: Bulgarian nationalist activists again obstructed vehicles arriving from Turkey at Kapitan Andreevo on 24 March 2017, targeting buses carrying Bulgarian citizens returning to vote. Passengers could walk across, and police removed the barricades so traffic resumed the same day. This was a protest against electoral travel, not an official prohibition on entry, and it followed a separate blockade earlier that week.

verification.notes: Checked March 24 event date rather than later publication, pedestrian alternative and same-day clearance.

summary: The Republic of Cyprus suspended passage at Deryneia, Astromeritis–Zodhia and Lefka–Apliki on 29 February 2020 as a COVID-19 precaution. It reopened these Green Line posts on 21 June for Cypriot citizens, residence-permit holders and other eligible groups, with testing requirements and humanitarian exceptions. The change did not restore access for every foreign visitor or remove Turkish Cypriot-side controls. Ledra Street remained closed under a separate timetable.

verification.notes: Checked authority-side suspension, three named posts, conditional June reopening and de facto-divide scope.

summary: Turkish Cypriot authorities closed the Limnitis–Kato Pyrgos Green Line crossing in March 2020 under COVID-19 measures. Passenger passage resumed on 26 June with testing requirements. A separate dispute over changed testing rules blocked some Kato Pyrgos commuters’ return journeys on 6 July; an agreed arrangement was reported on 9 July. That later incident affected particular commuters and does not extend the original closure or establish a complete shutdown of the crossing.

verification.notes: Checked actual June resumption, distinct July commuter refusals and policy resolution without inventing first resumed passage.

summary: Slovakia barred entry by most nonresident foreigners at its Austrian, Czech, Hungarian and Ukrainian borders from 13 March 2020 to limit COVID-19; the rule extended to Poland on 17 March. Citizens, residents, qualifying commuters and freight retained exceptions. Travel with participating neighbouring countries eased in June, while Ukrainian travellers faced different arrangements. Later permission for vaccinated Ukrainians does not establish one unchanged closure lasting until that date.

verification.notes: Checked four-frontier and Poland starts and cohort-specific easing; no universal Ukraine endpoint.

summary: Moldova restricted entry by nonexempt foreigners through its Ukrainian and Romanian land borders from 17 March 2020 to control COVID-19. Residents, transport crews, diplomats and authorised cases could still enter. From September, arrivals from lower-risk countries were allowed while restrictions continued for higher-risk origins. On 5 March 2021, the remaining origin-based exclusion was replaced by quarantine-based admission rules, rather than by removal of every health requirement.

verification.notes: Checked September green/red split and March 2021 repeal, distinct from later certificate removal.

summary: France restricted entry by travellers outside authorised categories at its internal European borders from 18 March 2020 during the first COVID-19 wave. Citizens, residents, cross-border workers and transport personnel retained exceptions, with additional family and work permissions introduced later. Ordinary leisure entry from most European neighbours resumed on 15 June. The Spanish frontier followed a separate timetable, and the admission restriction did not mean every physical crossing was sealed.

verification.notes: Checked March onset, inbound exceptions, June formal endpoint and Spanish-frontier exclusion.
